core_obligations: Reformulate K-flatness (proof lines 3089-3090): by the cited same-chapter lemma, a complex is K-flat exactly when the derived tensor product with it is an exact functor, so the assertion becomes a two out of three statement for exactness.

Use the triangle (proof lines 3090-3093): in a distinguished triangle in K(Mod(O)), if two out of three complexes are acyclic then so is the third, because the long exact cohomology sequence vanishes wherever two of its three terms do.
Conclude (proof line 3093): exactness is a two out of three property for the functors given by the three vertices of the triangle, so K-flatness is two out of three as asserted.
proof_roadmap: Translate K-flatness into exactness of the derived tensor product functor.
Observe that acyclicity is two out of three in a distinguished triangle.
Transfer that to exactness of the three functors, which is again two out of three.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that K-flatness is a two out of three property for a distinguished triangle in the homotopy category of complexes of modules on a ringed site (statement lines 3080-3086). The proof is a two-line reduction: the cited same-chapter lemma turns K-flatness of a complex into exactness of the derived tensor product functor with it, and the standard two out of three property for acyclicity in a distinguished triangle transfers to exactness of the three functors (proof lines 3089-3093). The content is the choice of the right reformulation, not a computation. The claim is H2: one reformulation plus one standard fact.
